report.summary: Chunk 2 of shape.py: describe() fallback cases, ShapeConflict dataclass, compare_declared() function.

handoff.purpose: Implement fallback type handlers in describe() and define ShapeConflict + compare_declared() for shape comparison.

symbols.name: describe
symbols.note: Fallback cases for dict, dataclass, __slots__, sequences, str/bytes/bytearray, scalar/None, and opaque.

symbols.name: ShapeConflict.agrees
symbols.note: Returns True if comparable and no undeclared_in_observation.

symbols.name: compare_declared
symbols.note: Compares observed shape names against declared field names.

claims.why: The dict branch returns names from keys and sets element to None, confirming keys are the focus.
Shape note explicitly says 'keys only; no value was recorded'.
The code returns Shape with note='dataclass fields'.
The code returns Shape with note='__slots__'.
The sequences branch returns length and element from next(iter(obj)).
The str/bytes branch returns Shape with note='length only; no content recorded'.

claims.text: no shape could be characterised for this type
claims.why: The opaque branch returns Shape with that note.

claims.text: missing_in_observation is the softest signal — these inputs did not exercise that field.
claims.why: The docstring describes missing_in_observation; the field exists and is used in compare_declared.

claims.text: undeclared_in_observation is the sharp one: the object carries something the code never declared, so the declaration is incomplete or the payload has undocumented shape.
claims.why: The field undeclared_in_observation exists and is populated in compare_declared.

claims.text: Refuses to compare rather than manufacturing findings: an observation with no names (a scalar, an unstructured array, an opaque object) is comparable=False with a reason.
claims.why: The function returns ShapeConflict with comparable=False when declared is empty or shape.names is empty.

claims.text: Reporting every declared field as 'missing' because the observation carries no names at all would turn 'we learned nothing here' into a wall of false positives.
claims.why: The function returns comparable=False without populating missing_in_observation when shape.names is empty.

claims.text: 'missing' below cannot be trusted while the list is clipped
claims.why: When shape.truncated is True, notes include this warning and missing_in_observation is set to ().

observations.what: The dict branch uses _names_of with a generator that calls red(k) but does not handle redact=False case; red is a parameter of describe, not defined locally.
The dict branch sets element to None even if depth < MAX_DEPTH and obj is non-empty; it only probes the first value's shape.
The sequences branch uses next(iter(obj)) which may raise StopIteration if obj is empty, but it's guarded by len(obj) check.
compare_declared uses sorted(set(...)) on declared_names, which may lose ordering but that's fine for set comparison.
The 'missing_in_observation' is set to () when shape.truncated is True, but the docstring warning is appended; this could hide real missing fields when truncated.
